title: Pleasant and unpleasant feelings
subtitle: content, thrilled, fed up, furious
summary: Describe how you feel with precision - content, grateful, delighted, miserable, fed up, frustrated, thrilled or furious - and grade those adjectives correctly.

lesson.heading: Happy feelings
lesson.text: You feel **content(ed)** when you are satisfied with what you have, **grateful** when someone has done something thoughtful for you, and **delighted** when something happens that gives you great pleasure.

examples.text: He's very **content** with his life. He's always been a **contented** person.
examples.note: Content is not used before a noun: a contented person, not ~~a content person~~.

examples.text: I'm really **grateful** to you for helping me with my project.
I was **delighted** to hear you're getting married.
I felt so **thankful** that nothing bad had happened.
examples.note: You feel thankful when something bad that could have happened did not happen.

lesson.heading: Unhappy feelings
lesson.text: You feel **miserable** when everything seems wrong, **discontented** when your life is not giving you satisfaction, and **depressed** when you are miserable over a long period of time.

examples.text: I felt **miserable** all day yesterday - maybe it was just the grey, cold weather.
She's very **discontented** with her job and is going to look for a new one.
I felt **depressed** after having ten job interviews and not getting a job.
examples.note: Depression is considered an illness in some severe cases.

lesson.heading: Had enough, or lost the thread
lesson.text: You feel **fed up** or **sick and tired** when you have had enough of something disagreeable, and **confused** when you cannot make sense of conflicting feelings or ideas.

examples.text: I'm **fed up** with Olivia's rudeness, and **sick and tired** of her bad behaviour.
I feel so **confused** - last week she said she loved me passionately; this week she said we were just good friends.

lesson.heading: Excitement, upset, anger and anxiety
rows: **inspired**
stimulated to do something positive or creative
I felt **inspired** after the concert. I've decided to take piano lessons.
**thrilled**
how you feel when something extremely exciting and pleasing happens
She was **thrilled** when she got a job with a TV company.
**upset**
made to feel unhappy
The argument I had with Eva really **upset** me.
**enthusiastic**
having very positive feelings
I was quite **enthusiastic** about my tennis lessons at first.
**frustrated**
feeling unable to do something you really want to do
The teacher isn't very good and now I just feel **frustrated**.
**nervous**
a bit like excited, but a negative feeling
I was so **nervous** before the exam.
**anxious**
afraid and uncertain
I felt **anxious** before the results came out.
**furious**
extremely angry
I was **furious** with the waiter - he spilt coffee over my shirt.

lesson.heading: How to grade these adjectives

right.label: Less extreme adjectives
right.text: Use a bit or quite, where quite means rather.

lesson.note: Really can be used with all the adjectives on this page.

lesson.text: Watch the prepositions: grateful to someone for something, fed up with something, sick and tired of something, furious with someone.

exercises.prompt: Who feels what? Match each remark with the feeling.

pairs.left: I've had enough of all the arguments at work.
I've been so unhappy for a long time. I've been seeing a psychiatrist.
I like my life and I have nothing to complain about.
Thank you for helping me today.
I'm just not feeling very happy today. Everything seems to have gone wrong.
I felt so good that nothing bad had happened. It could have been a disaster.

exercises.prompt: Match each remark with the feeling.

pairs.left: I just don't understand. Was that his wife or his daughter?
I felt very happy when I heard she had an interview for the job.
The service was slow and he spilt coffee over my shirt.
After six weeks of lessons I still can't play a single song.
After the concert I decided to take piano lessons.

exercises.prompt: After watching the nature programme, I felt ___ to become a zoologist.
exercises.explanation: Inspired means stimulated to do something positive or creative.

exercises.prompt: I always get ___ just before an exam.
exercises.explanation: Nervous is a bit like excited, but it is a negative feeling.

exercises.prompt: I was ___ when they refused to give me my money back.
exercises.explanation: Furious is the extreme form of angry.

exercises.prompt: I was ___ to see my old school friend again after so long.
exercises.explanation: You feel thrilled when something extremely exciting and pleasing happens.

exercises.prompt: The news about Rory's illness really ___ me.
exercises.explanation: To upset someone is to make them feel unhappy.

exercises.prompt: At first, I was ___ about the course, but it's just not very good.
exercises.explanation: Enthusiastic means having very positive feelings about something.

exercises.prompt: Are these positive or negative feelings?
I was feeling quite ___ because she had not phoned to say she had arrived safely.
exercises.explanation: Anxious describes being afraid and uncertain about what will happen.

exercises.prompt: I am absolutely sick and ___ of her selfish behaviour. I've had enough!
exercises.explanation: Sick and tired of is an extreme phrase, so it takes absolutely.

exercises.prompt: It's all so complicated. I feel a bit ___. Can you help me?
exercises.explanation: Confused is not an extreme adjective, so a bit or quite fits.

exercises.prompt: I was absolutely ___ when I heard the wonderful news!
exercises.explanation: Thrilled is an extreme adjective, so absolutely is the right adverb.

exercises.prompt: It made me feel quite ___ that I still couldn't play any songs after six weeks of guitar lessons.
exercises.explanation: Frustrated is feeling unable to do something you really want to do.

exercises.prompt: You always seem so ___ with life. How lucky you are!
exercises.hint: (adjective beginning with c, used before with)
exercises.explanation: Content or contented means satisfied with what you have.

exercises.prompt: Which adverb goes naturally with furious?
exercises.explanation: Furious is an extreme adjective, so it takes absolutely, not a bit.

exercises.statement: She is a very content person and never complains.
exercises.explanation: False - content is not used before a noun: She is a very contented person.
